text.p: Franco-German helicopter firm Eurocopter reaffirmed a break-even target for 1997, with a 300 million franc loss in 1996, its chairman said on Wednesday.

"Our plan was to return to break-even at the end of 1997, with a loss of 300 million francs in 1996. Currently, we have every reason to think these figures will be confirmed," Jean-Francois Bigay told a news conference.
He said 1997 had started with signs of hesitant growth after four years of collapse in the world helicopter market.
Eurocopter is 70 percent held by French state-owned Aerospatiale, 30 percent by Daimler-Benz Aerospace.
The appreciation of the dollar favours the competitiveness of Eurocopter, which is in the midst of a two-year restructuring based on a dollar at five francs, Bigay said.
Eurocopter has conservatively estimated new orders for 1997 of at least 150 helicopters, and around 150 for deliveries.

It expects 1997 sales to be evenly split between civil and military orders in value terms, resuming the more traditional division. Sales for 1996 were unusual in that 64 percent of value were in the military sector, with 36 in the civil segment.
Bigay said Eurocopter was "close to an agreement" with Turkey for an order for 30 Super Puma military aircraft.
The Turkish order would involve making some of the machines under licence, Bigay said.
The sale is worth around two billion francs, a senior Eurocopter executive said.

Eurocopter expects turnover for 1997 and 1998 to be higher, Bigay said, but gave no estimates. It delivered 165 aircraft last year and the estimated 1996 turnover of 9.3 billion francs was stable against 1995.
The 228 new aircraft orders received last year were worth 5.7 billion francs, the senior executive said.

The military market is still falling and Eurocopter wants to secure its market share in 1997. Eurocopter says in 1996 it won 20 percent of world military sales in units and 26 percent in value, regaining levels it last held in 1992 and 1993.
It held its market share in the civil market, which is showing an upturn.
